column1: # CI budgets (#1437). The only place a number is typed: `ci_budget_report.sh` reads this file
# and compares it with a run's own jobs, and the verdict is its exit status.
#   stage <TAB> budget_minutes <TAB> set_at <TAB> set_from
# `set_from` is the measurement the number came from, quoted with its run id. A budget without
# one cannot be compared to the number it should be, so it is not a check — the report fails on
# the row rather than on the run.
# **A budget is set from the worst run measured so far, rounded up.** Not from the mean: two runs
# of the same workflow on the same commit shape differ by 0.4-1.3 minutes per stage (coverage
# 15.3 → 16.4, audit 5.3 → 6.6, integration 14.9 → 15.6), so a budget set to the best observation
# fires on noise and is ignored within a week. A breach then means one thing: slower than anything
# that has been measured. Both runs quoted below are on `main`, both green.
# The ratchet has two halves, and both are enforced by `ci_budget_report.sh --base <ref>`:
#   · a budget may be **lowered** after a win, freely — that is the point;
#   · a budget may **not be raised** unless `set_from` changes too, which is how a raise names
#     what regressed instead of quietly moving the line;
#   · a row may not be deleted. A removed budget makes a breach invisible, not fixed.
# Every row was set from run 42229151064 (`ef77fb58`) and run 42359491268 (`08062df8`): wall
# 43.5 / 44.7 min, 159.4 / 164.7 job-minutes. A matrix stage is priced on its **slowest leg**,
# because that is what a stage costs in wall clock; its runner time is the sum of the legs and is
# priced only by TOTAL_JOB_MINUTES.
# `build` had a row and lost it with the job (#1438): six `cargo check` legs and a `check_*.sh`
# loop, 28-34 job-minutes, no artifact, five stages waiting on it. That deletion is what children
# 3-5 build on; when they land, every row here drops and the totals follow.
# The epic's targets (#1436) are lower than these numbers on purpose: ≤ 22 min wall, ≤ 70
# job-minutes, ≤ 10 min at p50. Children 2-4 earn them by removing work, and each win lowers a
# row here. Setting the ceiling to a target nobody has measured yet would fail on the first push.
